grh_99d7189e13230a3218b4.title: Words at War 44-01-11 (31) Eighty-Three Days - the Survival of Seaman Izzi
paragraphs: After a torpedo sinks his ship in the South Atlantic, Seaman Basil Izzi and a handful of survivors crowd onto a raft with almost no food or water. Over eighty-three days they endure hunger, thirst, storms, injuries, deaths and the repeated heartbreak of aircraft and ships passing without seeing them. As the men weaken, Izzi watches companions die and struggles to remain conscious himself. On the eighty-third day, an American patrol craft finally spots the raft and rescues the survivors, who are carried aboard and slowly nursed back to health.

This [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]] broadcast aired on January 11, 1944. It is listed as episode 31 in the archive. [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Paul Mann, [[person|lon-clark|Lon Clark]], Sam Wanamaker, Paul Gordon, and Milton Herman. Other credited names include Anton M. Leader as director, Edith Sommer as radio adaptor, and Jack Costello as host.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes.
This version dramatizes [[work|work.words.bd8779c474ab11a5|Eighty-Three Days - the Survival of Seaman Izzi]]. Mark Murphy is credited as author and Edith Sommer adapted it for radio.

Other versions or closely related recordings in the archive include [[episode|grh_039b12f33bb6be02ec0d|Words at War 43-10-05 (17) Eighty-Three Days - the Survival of Seaman Izzi]] (October 5, 1943), another recording of the same script.

grh_999186b47dbf64d388a7.title: White Out
paragraphs: Ski patrol captain Skip Blanchard warns resort owner Haverly that a whiteout is moving into Keyhole Basin and urges him to shut down the lifts, but the warning is ignored. Two inexperienced women, Lisa and Cindy, are carried to an expert slope just as the storm closes in and leaves them stranded in freezing wind and near-zero visibility. They attempt to descend through the trees while the patrol tracks their route. When the sky finally begins to clear, the women unknowingly ski onto an avalanche field just as rescuers reach them and the slope breaks loose. The patrol gets them through the slide alive, and afterward the women are ready to confront Haverly about the resort's safety practices.

The cast includes Joan McCall, Linda Kay Henning, Tommy Cook, Vic Perrin, and Shepard Menken. Other credited names include Elliott Lewis as director, Elliott Lewis as producer, Bruce Martin as writer, and Richard Widmark as host.
The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.9b0a0ccffce2f7d3|Sears, Roebuck and Company]].

grh_994721e0ec61f76332b3.title: Boy Meets Girl
paragraphs: Hollywood writers Benson and Law seize on pregnant studio waitress Susie as the answer to their latest story problem, then turn her baby Happy into a wildly successful screen attraction. Their meddling makes Susie's private life part of the studio machine, especially when star Larry Toms decides marrying Susie would give him control of Happy. The writers recruit English extra Rodney as part of another scheme, only to discover he genuinely loves Susie; after the confusion clears, Rodney and Susie are free to build a real family while the writers move on to their next racket.

grh_99325c6357a2764185d3.title: Birthday
paragraphs: Jeff Smith is determined to treat the day his wife Betty is due to give birth as an ordinary working day, even insisting they save money on flowers and that he return to the office rather than wait at the hospital.
